1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e3 Be7 5.cxd.strategy: Develops the bishop onto the diagonal aimed at the kingside, with the e3 pawn solid behind it. White keeps both plans of the structure open, central and kingside play on one hand and the queenside minority attack on the other, and decides later which to follow.

Castles to safety before White's pieces become active; the f6 knight guards h7, so the bishop on d3 is not a threat yet. Black's position is compact and sound, and Black regroups with the e-file and the break ...c5 as the main sources of counterplay.
